rules.description: Special Leave Petition (Civil) under Article 136 against a civil judgment, decree, determination or order. Cause title or cover says SLP (C), SLP (Civil), or Special Leave Petition (Civil). Not a civil appeal, writ, review, or miscellaneous application.

Special Leave Petition (Criminal) under Article 136 in a criminal proceeding. Cause title or cover says SLP (Crl.), SLP (Criminal), or Special Leave Petition (Criminal). Not a criminal appeal, writ, or review.
Civil Appeal to the Supreme Court of India, including an appeal by High Court certificate or an armed forces tribunal civil appeal. Cause title or cover says Civil Appeal or C.A. Not an SLP (Civil).
Criminal Appeal to the Supreme Court of India. Cause title or cover says Criminal Appeal or Crl.A. Not an SLP (Criminal).
Writ Petition (Civil) under Article 32 of the Constitution for enforcement of fundamental or other civil rights. Cause title or cover says Writ Petition (Civil) or W.P.(C).
Writ Petition (Criminal) under Article 32 involving personal liberty or a criminal matter. Cause title or cover says Writ Petition (Criminal) or W.P.(Crl.).

Transfer Petition (Civil) seeking transfer of a civil case from one High Court or court to another, typically under Article 139A of the Constitution or Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Cause title or cover says Transfer Petition (Civil) or T.P.(C).

Transfer Petition (Criminal) seeking transfer of a criminal case from one court to another, typically under Section 406 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Cause title or cover says Transfer Petition (Criminal) or T.P.(Crl.).
Review Petition (Civil) under Article 137 seeking review of a Supreme Court civil judgment. Cause title or cover says Review Petition (Civil) or R.P.(C). Not a curative petition.
Review Petition (Criminal) under Article 137 seeking review of a Supreme Court criminal judgment. Cause title or cover says Review Petition (Criminal) or R.P.(Crl.). Not a curative petition.
Original Suit in the Supreme Court under Article 131, typically a dispute between the Union and a State or between States. Cause title or cover says Original Suit or O.S.
Contempt Petition (Civil) for civil contempt of the Supreme Court or of its orders. Cause title or cover says Contempt Petition (Civil) or Cont.P.(C).
Contempt Petition (Criminal) for criminal contempt of the Supreme Court. Cause title or cover says Contempt Petition (Criminal) or Cont.P.(Crl.).
Election Petition in the Supreme Court, including a Presidential or Vice-Presidential election petition. Cause title or cover says Election Petition.

Arbitration Petition in the Supreme Court under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, typically for appointment of an arbitrator or a related arbitration proceeding. Cause title or cover says Arbitration Petition or Arb.P.
Curative Petition (Civil) filed after dismissal of a review petition in a civil matter. Cause title or cover says Curative Petition (Civil). Not a review petition.
Curative Petition (Criminal) filed after dismissal of a review petition in a criminal matter. Cause title or cover says Curative Petition (Criminal). Not a review petition.

Miscellaneous Application (M.A.) or Interlocutory Application (I.A.) in a pending Supreme Court matter, including restoration, clarification, modification, listing, or a similar application. Cause title or cover says M.A., I.A., Miscellaneous Application, or Interlocutory Application. Not a fresh SLP, appeal, writ, review, or curative petition.

petition_type.description: Petition type as printed, e.g. Special Leave Petition (Civil) or Transfer Petition (Civil). Fill from the Main Petition cause title first. If not printed there, fill from the Cover Page cause title. Check spelling against the other.

cause_title.description: Cause title representing petitioner vs respondent. Fill from Cover Page. If Cover Page is not in this pack, fill from the Main Petition caption and draft formatted_title from party counts.

advocates_on_record.description: Printed AOR footer only. Leave a field null if it is not printed; do not invent name, code, email, mobile, firm, chamber, or PIN. Do not copy petitioner or respondent names or addresses. Prefer Vakalatnama. If Vakalatnama is not in this pack or prints no AOR, use the Memo of Appearance footer, then the last page of the Main Petition (very end: Drawn By, Filed on, DRAWN & FILED BY, Advocate for Petitioner/Respondent, Chamber lines under the name). Do not use Main Petition opening or party-list pages. If office_address is still blank, last page of Listing Proforma / Proforma for First Listing. Remaining blanks: AOR's Certificate signature / DRAWN & FILED BY and Advocate's Checklist. Never override Vakalatnama.
advocates_on_record.title: Advocates On Record

impugned_orders.description: Primary impugned order only. Fill from the Impugned Order PDF if it is in this pack. If it is not attached, fill from bracketed particulars on the Main Petition cause title, Cover Page, AOR's Certificate, and Affidavit. If the same order appears in several of those, keep the Impugned Order PDF values when present; otherwise keep one consistent set and record mismatches in inconsistencies.
impugned_orders.title: Impugned Orders

relief_sort.description: Main prayer body only from the Main Petition last 2-3 pages. Copy the text under the heading Main Prayer or Prayer. Do not include the heading, clause number, markdown, or HTML (for example omit '7. MAIN PRAYER:' and '<u>**MAIN PRAYER**</u>:'). Start at the prayer sentence, e.g. 'In the circumstances stated above…'. Leave null if that heading is not printed.
relief_sort.title: Relief Sort

petition_date.description: Date of this petition from the last page of the Main Petition, after the heading Main Prayer or Prayer. Use the date printed next to Date, Date Drafted, or Date Filed on. If both Date Drafted and Date Filed on are printed, use only the Date Drafted date. Return the date as printed, without the label. Do not use a date inside the prayer, an impugned-order date, or a date from any other document. Leave null if none of those labels is printed after the prayer.
petition_date.title: Petition Date

inconsistencies.description: Spelling mismatches between fill and verify sources, plus an ORGANIZATION party with no acting_through. Always include a letter-level mismatch of the Cause Title main petitioner or main respondent versus petitioner 1 / respondent 1 on the Main Petition starting pages (e.g. Shalija vs Shailja). Cover Page has only one name per side; extra parties continue on later starting pages. Also flag when that Cause Title person is missing on those pages, is a different person than petitioner 1 / respondent 1, or is listed on the other side. Extra parties are not a mismatch against Cover Page And Anr/Ors. Also record Impugned Order case number, date, or forum mismatches across Impugned Order, Main Petition, Cover Page, AOR's Certificate, and Affidavit. Also record printed AOR chamber/office address mismatches across Vakalatnama, Memo of Appearance, Main Petition last page, Listing Proforma last page, and AOR's Certificate. Quote both printed strings. Do not invent an address. Ignore extra Ph. on the same chamber line. Party-name items[].raw_text is Cause Title: "Name"; Main Petition: "Name". items[].id is '1', '2', ….

data_schema.title: LegalExtractRecord

categories.name: Advocate's Checklist
categories.description: The current Supreme Court petition's numbered YES/NO/N.A. advocate checklist, often headed ADVOCATE'S CHECK LIST TO BE CERTIFIED BY ADVOCATE ON RECORD (also CHECK LIST, CHECKLIST, CHECK-LIST, or OCR variants with punctuation/spacing between letters). It verifies this petition against Supreme Court filing requirements such as limitation, court fee, number of copies, and annexure certification. Keep its numbered questions and continuation pages together, including a final date and AOR/Advocate signature or details page. Do NOT use this category for a government, registry, or tribunal form or circular merely titled Check List; keep it in its enclosing Annexure or Appendix.

categories.name: Cover Page
categories.description: The outer title sheet of the Supreme Court paper book, usually one page, with IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA at the top, JURISDICTION on the next line, and advocate for the petitioner or respondent at the foot. Often includes the words PAPER BOOK, {COVER PAGE}, and For Index Please See Inside above the advocate's name.

categories.name: Record of Proceedings
categories.description: This Court's record of proceedings, usually a one-page table of hearing dates and orders, headed RECORD OF PROCEEDING or RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS.

categories.name: AOR's Certificate
categories.description: The Advocate-on-Record (AOR) certificate in the paper book. Use only when the page opens with this case's full Supreme Court cause title (party names and VERSUS), immediately followed by CERTIFICATE (including letter-spaced text), and the AOR / Advocate-on-Record's own certification such as Certified that the petition is confined to pleadings before the court whose order is challenged. It usually ends FILED ON or DRAWN & FILED BY. A certificate or registration certificate within an Annexure, Appendix, Checklist, or another form remains part of that document. A Listing Proforma signature block is not this category.

categories.name: Index
categories.description: The paper-book Index: the consecutive page run of the table of PARTICULARS OF DOCUMENT and PAGE NO, usually headed INDEX. Keep every page of that same table together in physical PDF order, from its first page through its final continuation page. Do not split an Index page into Annexure, Appendix, Application, Filing Memo, Vakalatnama, or another document just because the Index lists or mentions it; those are row entries, not page headings. The Index can start at different PDF page numbers; pages 1–10 are common, not a required range. A Master Index and a volume-specific Index are each Index sections; start a distinct run only when a new Index table actually begins after a different section. Filing Index / Index of Filing is Filing Memo only when it is a standalone filing list, not a row or page within the paper-book Index.

categories.name: Office Report on Limitation
categories.description: The Supreme Court of India's Registry Office Report on Limitation (O/R on Limitation) for this Supreme Court petition, stating whether it is within time and any delay in filing or re-filing. Confirm the report belongs to the Supreme Court proceeding from its court/registry heading and matching case details. A High Court or tribunal Office Report on Limitation reproduced in this compiled filing is part of its enclosing Annexure, not this Supreme Court paper-book section, even though it has the same title.

categories.name: Listing Proforma
categories.description: The first-listing proforma, identified by its form structure as well as any heading. Headings may read PERFORMA, PROFORMA, PERFORMA FOR FIRST LISTING, PROFORMA FOR FIRST LISTING, PROFORMA OF FIRST LISTING, LISTING PROFORMA, LISTED PROFORMA, or similar variants; no one heading is required. The defining pattern is a series of left-hand prompts/numbered keys with corresponding values, such as Central/State Act, section and rule; impugned-order date, High Court, judges or tribunal/authority; nature of matter; petitioner/respondent names and contacts; main/sub-classification; listing restrictions; similar disposed or pending cases; and applicable criminal, land-acquisition, tax, special-category, or vehicle details. 'SECTION XII' and 'The case pertains to' may appear but are not required. Treat consecutive pages with this same form structure as one Listing Proforma, even when the heading is absent from continuation pages. It ends with its date and AOR/Advocate-on-Record details and signature (for example, name, party represented, AOR/CC code, email, mobile, or chamber address); keep that closing page in the Listing Proforma. It is not an AOR's Certificate.

categories.name: Synopsis
categories.description: The narrative SYNOPSIS section, starting at the SYNOPSIS heading and continuing across its lettered pages (for example, B-L) until a separate LIST OF DATES, LIST OF DATES AND EVENTS, or LIST OF EVENTS heading belonging to this Supreme Court petition. Stop Synopsis at that heading. From the heading onward, classify the dated event table and its continuation pages (for example, M-V) as List of Dates & Events, even if the split model initially labels them Synopsis. Do not use a lettered folio, mentions of dates/events, or references to other filing documents alone to change the section; use the explicit heading and the page content. Synopsis pages are narrative, while List of Dates pages are organized as chronological date/event entries. A LIST OF EVENTS with a High Court/tribunal caption and different case number inside an Annexure belongs to that Annexure, not this Synopsis.

categories.name: List of Dates & Events
categories.description: A chronological LIST OF DATES, LIST OF DATES & EVENTS, or LIST OF EVENTS in the current Supreme Court petition, with a date before each event. Dates may use DD/MM/YYYY, MM/YYYY, or YY. Only the first page carries the heading; continue the same dated entries across pages. A date entry mentioning an Annexure remains part of List of Dates, not that Annexure. A lower-court LIST OF EVENTS with its own court caption/case number inside a reproduced record remains in its enclosing Annexure.

categories.name: Main Petition
categories.description: This case's main Supreme Court petition body. Identify it by the Supreme Court cause title and this case's own petition number, followed by this case's party details (often Between, names/addresses/relationships, and positions before the High Court and this Court; other petition formats may use a different party layout). SLPs generally use Form 28; other petition types need not. It contains the petition's own pleadings and ends with its Prayer, drafting/filing date, and advocate/AOR details. Keep Applications separate even when their closing Prayer and signature block look similar. A High Court/tribunal petition or order reproduced inside an Annexure, with a different court or case number, stays in that Annexure despite its own Grounds, Prayer, or SHOWETH section.

categories.name: Affidavit
categories.description: The main affidavit for this Supreme Court petition, usually headed AFFIDAVIT, with a Deponent, Verification, and notary/oath attestation. Match its case type/cause title to the Cover Page and Main Petition and use its place in the outer paper-book sequence. An affidavit from an earlier proceeding inside an Annexure remains part of that Annexure, even if it has a deponent, verification, and attestation. A checklist or index mention of an affidavit is not an affidavit section.

categories.name: Annexures
categories.description: Case-specific supporting exhibits attached to the current Supreme Court petition. Use the Supreme Court paper-book Index and its page ranges as the authority for the outer P/R exhibit number. A reproduced High Court/tribunal record may contain local labels such as ANNEXURE NO. 1 or ANNEXURE 5; never treat those local numbers as Supreme Court P/R numbers or use them alone to create a new boundary. Preserve each outer Index-listed exhibit and its complete continuous document. If the Index, outer numbering, and document contents conflict and the correct boundary cannot be established without cutting through a document, do not guess or split that document: place the entire uncertain exhibit/document run in Unidentified and provide a plain-language reason naming the conflicting cues. Preserve actual series and numbers (for example P-10, P-20, P-50, R-2, or E-number variants mapped only when supported by the outer Index). Do not cap the sequence at 15 or renumber by position.

categories.name: Application
categories.description: A separate interlocutory/application document in this Supreme Court filing, usually introduced by APPLICATION or I.A. and beginning with RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH or MOST RESPECTFULLY SHEWETH. Keep each application and its continuation pages together. Number separate applications sequentially in filing order (Application 1, 2, 3, …) with no fixed limit; do not stop at 15. A page headed Annexure belongs to that numbered Annexure, not an Application.

categories.name: Appendix
categories.description: A separately headed APPENDIX containing supporting legal or reference material, commonly the English text of constitutional provisions, statutes, rules, regulations, orders, notifications, schedules, or bye-laws referred to in the challenged decision or petition. APPENDIX, APPENDIX I/II, APPENDIX-I, and lettered variants may be used. Distinguish it from an Annexure: an Appendix primarily supplies legal text relied on, while an Annexure is a case-specific record or document. Follow the explicit document label and paper-book boundaries; an Appendix reproduced within an Annexure P-n range remains part of that Annexure.

categories.name: Memo of Parties
categories.description: A distinct MEMO OF PARTIES or MEMORANDUM OF PARTIES section in the outer paper-book. Normally require the Supreme Court case identity and parties to match the current petition; a cause title or party list alone is not enough. A separate High Court Memo of Parties may be included in this section only when the outer paper-book Index lists it as a standalone back-matter document (for example, 'Memo of Parties in High Court') after the Filing Memo. A High Court/tribunal memo reproduced within an Annexure, or a party list embedded in an Application, stays with its enclosing document. Distinguish a standalone memo from the Main Petition cause title.

categories.name: Memo of Appearance
categories.description: A Memo of Appearance for this Supreme Court proceeding, with case-insensitive heading forms such as 'Memo of Appearance', 'Memo Of Appearance', 'MEMO OF APPEARANCE', or 'Memorandum of Appearance'; tolerate clear OCR/spelling variants such as 'Memo of Apprearance'. Record that an Advocate-on-Record, advocate, or party appears for a named party. Require the Supreme Court caption and matching current parties/case identity. A High Court/tribunal memo, or one reproduced within an Annexure or Application, stays with its enclosing document.

categories.name: Impugned Order
categories.description: The standalone copy of the judgment, order, decree, sentence, direction, or other decision that is the direct subject of challenge in this Supreme Court petition/appeal. Identify the challenged decision using the case papers together: give greatest weight to explicit statements naming the impugned/challenged decision or saying the petition is directed against it, and to the Prayer's requested relief; cross-check the court/authority, case number, date, and document type against the opening challenge, Synopsis/List of Dates, Grounds, and the order copy. The target may be a High Court, tribunal, trial court, or other authority decision depending on the procedural route; do not assume it is always a High Court order or simply the latest decision mentioned. Where multiple decisions are expressly challenged, keep the directly challenged order set together. Earlier or underlying decisions mentioned only as procedural history, background, or context are not Impugned Order. A different order reproduced inside an Annexure P-n remains part of that Annexure unless it is the standalone copy of a decision directly challenged in this petition. If no order copy is attached, do not classify the petition's references as an Impugned Order document; use those references only as particulars for extraction.

categories.name: Vakalatnama
categories.description: A VAKALATNAMA, VAKALAT NAMA, VAKALTNAMA, or clear OCR/spelling variant that appoints an Advocate-on-Record to act for a party in this Supreme Court petition. Require the Supreme Court caption and match the parties/case to the current petition; the standalone instrument in the outer paper-book sequence is the top-level section. Keep its accompanying Memo of Appearance with it: the memo commonly appears on the same page, and when it begins on the immediately following page, include that full continuation page in the combined Memo of Appearance + Vakalatnama document. A High Court/tribunal instrument, or one reproduced within an Annexure or Application, stays with that enclosing document. Distinguish it from PoA/BR (authorizes a representative).

categories.name: PoA/BR
categories.description: A Power of Attorney or Board Resolution establishing authority for a person to act for a party. Classify a Power of Attorney from its heading and instrument structure (grantor/principal authorizes or empowers an attorney/representative); do not infer it from the phrase 'power to act' alone. Classify a Board Resolution from corporate meeting/resolution structure, such as a board of directors and 'RESOLVED THAT' authorizing a named person to institute or conduct proceedings. Keep either separate from a Vakalatnama (appointment of counsel) and Memo of Appearance (record of appearance). Match the represented party to this petition and retain it as part of an enclosing Annexure when it is reproduced there.

categories.name: Filing Memo
categories.description: The current Supreme Court petition's Filing Memo: the filing-submission sheet for this case, commonly headed FILING MEMO and showing the Supreme Court caption/case particulars, filing AOR, papers filed, and date. Match the court and case identity to this petition. A High Court/tribunal Filing Memo or a filing slip reproduced within an Annexure or Application stays with its enclosing document; it is not the Supreme Court Filing Memo.

categories.name: Court Fees
categories.description: Court fee stamps or court-fee endorsement pages.

splitting_strategy.custom_instructions: REPRESENTATION DOCUMENTS: Vakalatnama, Memo of Appearance, and Memo of Parties are top-level only for the current Supreme Court case and outside an Annexure/Application. Match the Supreme Court caption and parties; copies or lower-court forms inside a marked annexure stay in that annexure. MEMO OF APPEARANCE headings are case-insensitive (Memo of Appearance, Memo Of Appearance, MEMO OF APPEARANCE, Memorandum of Appearance); accept clear OCR variants such as Apprearance. REPRESENTATION DOCUMENT SCOPE: recognize Vakalatnama and Memo of Appearance only for the current Supreme Court petition, matching its caption and parties. High Court/tribunal instruments and copies reproduced in an Annexure or Application stay with that enclosing section. Accept VAKALATNAMA, VAKALAT NAMA, VAKALTNAMA and clear OCR variants. FILING MEMO SCOPE: label Filing Memo only when its heading and Supreme Court caption/case particulars identify this current Supreme Court filing. A lower-court or tribunal filing memo, or one reproduced inside an Annexure/Application, stays in its enclosing section. MEMO OF PARTIES SCOPE: only the standalone memo matching this Supreme Court petition and its parties is a top-level Memo of Parties. High Court/tribunal memos, memos inside Annexures, and party lists inside Applications stay with their enclosing document. OUTER PAPER-BOOK IDENTITY: a lower-court application or other document reproduced inside an Annexure does not end that Annexure run. The Index is the Supreme Court paper-book's own opening table, usually before the SLP preface; an Index/Table of Contents reproduced inside an Annexure stays in that Annexure. The SLP's Synopsis and List of Dates & Events belong to this case and precede the standalone challenged order. In the outer Supreme Court petition, a LIST OF EVENTS heading can mark the List of Dates & Events boundary; a High Court/tribunal LIST OF EVENTS with a different case caption inside an Annexure remains part of that Annexure. Keep a reproduced High Court List of Events inside its Annexure. Identify the standalone Impugned Order by the challenged court, case number/date and judgment copy between this SLP's chronology and its Form 28 petition; mentions of an order in Synopsis/List of Dates are not the order copy. For Vakalatnama and Memo of Appearance, match the Supreme Court cause title/current parties and outer filing sequence; a High Court instrument reproduced inside an Annexure stays there. GENERAL RULE -- CONTINUATION PAGES: when a page continues the prose, numbered list, or table from the page immediately before it, and does not itself open with a new heading, cause title, ANNEXURE/APPENDIX/APPLICATION marker, or form title, keep it in the SAME category as the previous page -- even if its text contains words that resemble another category's name (CHECK LIST, CERTIFICATE, GROUNDS, PRAYER, ANNEXURE, IMPUGNED, AFFIDAVIT). This matters most inside Index, Synopsis, and List of Dates & Events, which print their heading only on the first page and then continue silently for several pages -- a mention of 'APPENDIX' or 'ANNEXURE-P/1' in an Index row, or of 'annexed as ANNEXURE-P/1' in a List of Dates entry, does not start a new segment. Near-blank scanned pages, such as blank backs or separator sheets, continue the preceding document instead of starting a new segment. ANNEXURES: use the Supreme Court paper-book Index and page ranges to determine outer exhibit identity. Preserve its series and number (including P-10, P-20, P-50, R-2, or E-number variants only when supported by the Index); do not cap the sequence at 15 or renumber by position. Local High Court/tribunal labels such as ANNEXURE NO. 1 are internal and never create outer P/R boundaries. Do not cut an exhibit or reproduced document at a local label. When the Index and content do not establish a safe match, keep the complete uncertain continuous run together in Unidentified and include the reason in its user-visible metadata. A lower-court petition inside an exhibit is not this case's Main Petition. APPLICATIONS: keep each separately headed APPLICATION / I.A. and its continuation pages as a distinct Application, numbered sequentially in filing order without a fixed maximum (Application 1, 2, 3, …). A page headed Annexure belongs to that numbered Annexure, not an Application. TYPICAL ORDER: Advocate's Checklist, Cover Page, Record of Proceedings, Index, Office Report on Limitation, Listing Proforma, Synopsis, List of Dates & Events, Impugned Order, Main Petition, AOR's Certificate, Affidavit, then Annexures, Appendix, Applications, Memo of Parties, Memo of Appearance, Vakalatnama, Filing Memo. Some filings omit sections from this order (a missing Impugned Order or Affidavit is a common filing defect) -- do not force a page into a category just to fill a gap in this sequence. OFFICE REPORT SCOPE: when processing a Supreme Court of India petition, label as Office Report on Limitation only the Supreme Court Registry report for this same petition. Check the court/registry heading and case details. A High Court or tribunal Office Report on Limitation included inside a reproduced proceeding belongs to its enclosing Annexure P-n, not the Supreme Court paper-book section; the shared title alone is insufficient. A page printed OFFICE REPORT ON LIMITATION is never a Cover Page, but it is not automatically the Supreme Court report. CHECKLIST/CERTIFICATE FALSE POSITIVES: a circular, government form, or registry document titled 'Check List' or 'Checklist' that is not itself verifying this filing against Supreme Court Rules (for example, a state government's list of documents required to register a cooperative society) is not Advocate's Checklist -- classify it as whichever Annexure or Appendix contains it. A page with the cause title at the top then CERTIFICATE or C E R T I F I C A T E is AOR's Certificate, not Main Petition, Cover Page, or Affidavit; CERTIFICATE is always printed on that page. The word CERTIFICATE appearing inside a government-issued certificate, a check-list circular, or any other Annexure content is NOT AOR's Certificate. Cause title without the word CERTIFICATE is Cover Page or Main Petition. NESTED PETITIONS AND ORDERS: a lower court, tribunal, or authority's order, judgment, or petition reproduced inside an Annexure P-n keeps that Annexure's category even if it independently contains its own GROUNDS, PRAYER, CERTIFICATE, or RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH/SHEWETH sections, or reads like a judgment. Only a cause title reading IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA with THIS case's own SLP/petition number marks Main Petition or Impugned Order; a caption reading IN THE HIGH COURT..., or naming a different Writ/Appeal/Revision/case number, marks that content as the surrounding Annexure instead. Main Petition is Form 28 in this Court; it appears once as contiguous pages and cannot reappear after it ends. SHARED PAGES: Split assigns one category per physical page. If Vakalatnama and Memo of Appearance share a page, retain that page in the combined Memo of Appearance + Vakalatnama output; if Memo of Appearance starts on the immediately following page, include that page in the same combined output. Do not create a boundary within a physical page. For other short documents sharing a page, use whichever heading appears first/higher. OCR-DEGRADED PAGES: some annexure pages are poorly scanned with garbled or partly unreadable text. Do not mark these uncategorized purely for that reason -- use their position between identified pages of the same Annexure, plus any partially legible heading or page-corner numbering, to keep them with their neighbors. INDEX OF FILING, FILING INDEX, or FILING MEMO is Filing Memo, not Index. NOTE-BASED DISAMBIGUATION: When cues conflict, use document sequence and case identity, not a title word alone. Main Petition: confirm this case's Supreme Court number/cause title and party block; other petition formats need not follow Form 28. Keep its own Prayer and closing date/signature with it. Applications can also end with Prayer and signatures, so start a separate Application at its own heading and follow its preceding contents. Main Affidavit: match cause title/case type to this petition and look for Deponent, Verification, and attestation; affidavits from earlier proceedings inside exhibits remain Annexure pages. Memo of Parties: match case type, number, order date, and court under challenge; a memo in an Annexure run remains that Annexure. Vakalatnama: match cause title and parties to the current petition; do not select one from an earlier proceeding just because it has the same heading. Impugned Order: use the standalone order for this case; earlier orders reproduced inside an Annexure remain there. Appendix begins at its APPENDIX heading. Court-fee pages are Court Fees. A Power of Attorney or Board Resolution is PoA/BR, not Vakalatnama. Index: distinguish the Master Index overview from volume-specific Indexes, keep separate runs distinct, and retain clearly associated index entries even if printed outside the table; Filing Memo remains separate. Keep the Checklist's closing compliance declaration, date, and AOR details with it. Listing Proforma likewise retains its closing date and available AOR signature/details; neither block is an AOR's Certificate. SYNOPSIS / LIST OF DATES BOUNDARY: Keep the narrative Synopsis from its SYNOPSIS heading through its consecutive continuation pages. When a separate LIST OF DATES or LIST OF DATES AND EVENTS heading appears, end Synopsis there and label that page and the following date/event table continuation pages List of Dates & Events. In a lettered sequence such as B-L followed by M-V, the heading marks the boundary: B-L can be Synopsis and M-V List of Dates & Events. Do not let Synopsis absorb the dated table, and do not treat ordinary dates or document references in Synopsis narrative as a List of Dates section. List of Dates accepts DD/MM/YYYY, MM/YYYY, and YY event dates; entries mentioning Annexures remain List of Dates. Within an Annexure P-n run, headings such as Certificate, Affidavit, Grounds, Prayer, or a lower-court caption do not by themselves start a paper-book section. REPRESENTATION PAIR: Vakalatnama and Memo of Appearance are one combined output. If Memo of Appearance is on the same page, retain the page; if it starts on the immediately following page, include that page in the combined output. LOCAL EXHIBIT NUMBERS: the Supreme Court Index defines outer Annexure numbers and page ranges. A lower-court record can carry local labels such as ANNEXURE NO. 1; do not convert these to Supreme Court P-n labels or cut the record at those internal labels. If Index identity or the boundary remains uncertain, keep the complete continuous document together in Unidentified and include a plain-language reason in the Unidentified part metadata shown to the user.
